title: QMaxCal: Path-Space Regularization for Open Quantum Control via Girsanov's Theorem
abstract: arXiv:2606.19947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable quantum control in the presence of decoherence requires policies that combat the effect of environmental noise on the controlled dynamics. Open quantum systems under continuous monitoring generate classical measurement records whose drift depends on the noise experienced by the system; the records of two evolutions sharing the same decoherence channels differ only in this drift, so Girsanov's theorem yields a closed-form, differentiable estimator of the KL divergence between their trajectory distributions. We instantiate this estimator with two physically motivated reference measures, yielding two regularizers that both drive the system toward states where the effects of decoherence are minimal: the Wiener KL (KL_W), which is empirically more effective under certain conditions on the noise model, and the drift-variance regularizer (R_DV), which works for all noise models. Both are qualitatively distinct from existing penalties on control fluence or smoothness: they penalize the observable consequences of control on the decoherence channels rather than the control amplitude itself. The regularizers outperform unregularized gradient-based and reinforcement-learning baselines across a range of open quantum systems -- including single- and multi-qubit benchmarks and a multi-qubit chain calibrated to a published snapshot of the IBM Kingston processor -- along several axes of evaluation: final-state fidelity, robustness to mismatch in the assumed noise model (gains grow from +17 pp at training noise to +27 pp under 2.5x noise mismatch), and occupation of forbidden states. The regularizers reduce infidelity by up to 50%, with ~16% gains on the calibrated IBM Kingston chain.
authors: Merijn Moody, Zier Mensch, Miranda C. N. Cheng, Peter G. Bolhuis, Max Welling

ai_detailed_summary: 论文面向存在退相干和连续监测的开放量子系统，研究如何获得可靠的量子控制策略。作者利用 Girsanov 定理构造轨迹分布之间 KL 散度的闭式可微估计，并将其作为路径空间正则化。该方法用于约束或优化量子控制策略，使其更好地应对环境噪声。研究直接结合机器学习/优化思想与量子动力学控制，属于高度相关的 AI4Science。

title: Quantum ring all-reduce: communication and privacy advantages for distributed learning
abstract: arXiv:2606.20344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning models have scaled to unprecedented sizes, making training across distributed devices the de facto standard in the field. In this work, we explore how quantum communications can make distributed training both more communication-efficient and information-theoretically private, for both classical and quantum learning models. Ring all-reduce is the foundational communication primitive for large-scale distributed training. We present a quantum version that reduces per-link online communication by a provably optimal factor of two using pre-shared entanglement and superdense coding, without requiring the learning model or gradient computation to change. Beyond bandwidth, the primitive enables privacy guarantees that are information-theoretically impossible for any classical protocol, achieving composable ϵ-secure aggregation, via verified entanglement, at a 2x overhead in GHZ copies. Our hybrid quantum-classical communication architecture yields simultaneous communication and security advantages for large scale distributed training, regardless of whether the learning itself is quantum or classical. Finally, we characterise quantum advantages in gradient conflict detection for server-to-client communication under bandwidth constraints, a setting that arises after ring all-reduce is completed, when full gradient broadcast to external clients is infeasible. Two variants of the problem admit different separations. For margin-based alignment testing (textscGapIPτ), the quantum advantage is quadratic in the margin parameter: widetildeO(τ⁻¹łog P) qubits versus widetildeO(min(τ⁻²,P)) bits. For sign-consistency auditing against a private parameter matching (textscTieAuditϵ), the advantage represents an exponential separation in communication complexity: Ømega(sqrtP) bits whereas O(ϵ⁻²łog P) qubits suffice.

title: Topological Data Analysis for High-Dimensional Dynamic Process Monitoring
abstract: arXiv:2606.20443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time process monitoring requires methods that extract actionable information from high-dimensional time-series data. In this work, we present a new approach for process monitoring that combines tools of topological data analysis (TDA) and machine learning. In the proposed approach, we represent multivariate time-series data as manifolds and use topological descriptors to summarize the structure of such data; we then use a neural ordinary differential equation to learn the dynamic evolution of the topological structure of the system. Using real data from an industrial process, we show that this trajectory-based event detection approach is effective at detecting diverse types of events. We contrast this approach against reconstruction-based approaches such as principal component analysis and autoencoders and against a trajectory-based approach that uses Koopman autoencoders.
authors: Angan Mukherjee, Tyler A. Soderstrom, Michael J. Kurtz, Victor M. Zavala
ai_explanation: 该论文将拓扑数据分析、机器学习和神经 ODE 用于高维动态过程监测。动态过程建模和过程系统监测与计算科学、工程物理/化工过程数据驱动分析高度相关。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文提出一种高维时间序列过程监测方法，将多变量动态数据表示为流形，并用拓扑描述符总结其结构。随后使用神经常微分方程学习系统拓扑结构随时间的演化。该框架结合 TDA 与机器学习，面向实时过程监测中的异常或状态变化识别。其思想可用于化工过程、能源系统、制造与其他科学工程动态系统的数据驱动建模。

title: Entropy Estimation in Multi-Qutrit Systems via Variational and Classical Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2606.20504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a systematic study of von Neumann entropy estimation in multi-qutrit quantum systems using two complementary approaches: variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) and classical convolutional neural networks (CNNs), evaluated using an ideal (noise-free) quantum simulator. For systems up to three qutrits, we construct and evaluate 11 hardware-efficient SU(3)-inspired ansatzes. A parameter sweep shows that estimation accuracy is primarily determined by the number of trainable parameters, provided sufficient entanglement is present. Based on this study, we fix the parameter count to approximately 120 for subsequent experiments, observing that increasing entangling-gate counts beyond a threshold yields only marginal improvements. For larger systems (two to five qutrits), we use a CNN trained on measurement outcomes from tensor-product mutually unbiased bases. The model achieves accurate and stable predictions and exhibits a systematic improvement in performance with system size, with the highest errors for two-qutrit systems and the lowest for five-qutrit systems. Notably, using only 12.5% of the measurements required for full state tomography is sufficient to reach 90th-percentile absolute errors of approximately 0.13-0.16 nats for both four- and five-qutrit systems. The CNN model is also robust to shot noise and generalizes well to out-of-distribution states. Overall, within the simulated settings studied here, our results indicate a transition in practical methods: VQAs are effective for small systems, while CNN-based estimators offer improved scalability and robustness for larger qutrit systems.
authors: Sai Sakunthala Guddanti, Anil Prabhakar, Ria Rushin Joseph
ai_explanation: 该论文将变分量子算法和卷积神经网络用于多 qutrit 量子系统的冯诺依曼熵估计，明确属于 AI 与量子物理/量子计算交叉。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文研究多 qutrit 量子系统中的冯诺依曼熵估计问题。方法上比较了变分量子算法和经典卷积神经网络，并在理想量子模拟器上评估多种 SU(3) 启发的硬件高效 ansatz。结果表明估计精度主要受可训练参数数量影响，同时需要足够的纠缠结构。该工作体现了机器学习与量子信息、量子物理模拟的结合。

title: AK-MCS-C2 : Active Kriging Monte Carlo Simulation method with conformal certification for failure probability estimation
abstract: arXiv:2606.20191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a novel active-learning framework for failure probability estimation in structural reliability analysis that integrates Active Kriging Monte Carlo simulation with conformal prediction. The proposed approach employs an adaptive cross-conformal strategy specifically designed for small-sample settings and kriging surrogate models using the J+GP conformal estimator. Unlike standard AK-MCS methods, the proposed framework provides distribution-free guarantees on prediction errors, leading to more reliable classification of samples near the limit-state surface. This improved uncertainty quantification enhances both the accuracy and robustness of failure probability estimates, especially for rare-event regimes where such efficiency is crucial. Reproducible numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the method and also compare it to classical approaches on well-established benchmarks.
authors: Edgar Jaber (CB,ENS Paris Saclay), Vincent Chabridon (EDF R&D PRISME), Mathilde Mougeot (CB,ENSIIE,ENS Paris Saclay)
ai_explanation: 该论文将主动学习、Kriging 代理模型、蒙特卡洛模拟和保形预测用于结构可靠性失效概率估计，属于 AI/统计学习与工程科学计算交叉。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文研究结构可靠性分析中的失效概率估计问题。方法上结合 Active Kriging Monte Carlo Simulation 与 conformal prediction，在小样本条件下构建自适应代理模型。其目标是在极限状态边界附近更可靠地分类样本，并给出分布无关的预测误差保证。该工作与不确定性量化、工程仿真代理模型和科学计算密切相关。

title: Flow Matching for Efficient and Scalable Data Assimilation
abstract: arXiv:2508.13313v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Data assimilation (DA) estimates a dynamical system's state from noisy observations. Recent generative models like the ensemble score filter (EnSF) improve DA in high-dimensional nonlinear settings but are computationally expensive. We introduce the ensemble flow filter (EnFF), a training-free, flow matching (FM)-based framework that accelerates sampling and offers flexibility in flow design. EnFF uses Monte Carlo estimators for the marginal flow field, localized guidance for observation assimilation, and utilizes a novel flow path that exploits the Bayesian DA formulation. It generalizes classical filters such as the bootstrap particle filter and ensemble Kalman filter. Experiments on high-dimensional benchmarks demonstrate EnFF's improved cost-accuracy tradeoffs and scalability, highlighting FM's potential for efficient, scalable DA. Code is available at https://github.com/Utah-Math-Data-Science/Data-Assimilation-Flow-Matching.
authors: Taos Transue, Bohan Chen, So Takao, Bao Wang
ai_explanation: 该论文将 flow matching 生成模型用于数据同化，面向高维非线性动力系统状态估计，明确属于 AI 与科学计算/物理动力系统交叉。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文研究从噪声观测中估计动力系统状态的数据同化问题。作者提出 Ensemble Flow Filter，将 flow matching 引入数据同化，以替代计算代价较高的 score-based ensemble filter。方法包括边缘流场的蒙特卡洛估计、局部观测引导和新的流路径设计。该工作对天气、流体、地球系统等高维动力系统模拟具有潜在意义，属于典型 AI4Science。

title: GLARE: A Natural Language Interface for Querying Global Explanations
abstract: arXiv:2606.19735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While global explanations are crucial for understanding vision models across datasets, classes, and decision contexts, their complex and monolithic nature often hinders practical exploration. Because users typically seek targeted answers to specific questions rather than static artifacts, we present an LLM-based interactive interface that provides natural language access to global explanations for black-box image classifiers. The system's core LLM acts as a mediator, translating natural language questions into structured SQL queries over local explanation data. This enables flexible aggregation without exposing users to low-level representations. For each query, the interface outputs statistics-augmented natural language responses, supporting local explanations, and intent-aligned visualizations. We evaluate the system on intent interpretation, query mapping accuracy, generalization to novel queries and datasets, and robustness to linguistic errors. Our results demonstrate that LLM-mediated querying substantially improves the accessibility and usability of global explanations for human-centered XAI.
ai_explanation: 该论文提出面向图像分类器全局解释的自然语言查询接口。它属于可解释 AI 和视觉模型交互工具，未体现科学领域应用。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文提出 GLARE，一个基于 LLM 的交互式接口，使用户能够用自然语言查询黑盒图像分类器的全局解释。系统将自然语言问题转化为针对本地解释数据库的 SQL 查询。研究目标是让复杂、静态的全局解释更易探索和使用。虽然可解释性技术可潜在用于科学图像，但摘要没有具体科学对象，因此不判为 AI4Science 相关。

title: Grounded Inference: Principles for Deterministically Encapsulated Generative Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.19753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The incorporation of generative models into traditional computational systems presents both enormous opportunity and tremendous peril. Although many early adopters have realized these perils at great expense, the field still requires foundational frameworks to de-risk incorporation of AI into traditional systems. This manuscript establishes this foundation through the definition of four specific primitives of AI blended architecture, designed to enable deterministic encapsulation of probabilistic models. It further establishes two overarching anti-patterns broadly represented across industry to serve as warnings for engineers in this field. This framework was designed to enable successful integration of AI into traditional systems while providing a foundation upon which generative model providers could build the next generation of generative model interfaces.
ai_explanation: 该论文提出生成模型嵌入传统计算系统的架构原则，属于通用 AI 系统安全与工程框架，不针对物理、化学、材料或科学模拟问题。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文讨论如何将概率式生成模型确定性地封装进传统计算系统，以降低 AI 集成风险。作者定义了若干 AI blended architecture 的基本原语，并提出用于约束生成模型行为的原则。研究重点是软件架构、可靠性和系统设计。虽然涉及生成模型，但没有面向科学计算、物理建模、化学发现或材料设计的具体应用。

title: eCNNTO: A Highly Generalizable ConvNet for Accelerating Topology Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2606.19921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work proposes an element-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to accelerate density-based Topology Optimization (TO), termed eCNNTO. TO generally undergoes a large number of iterations, where finite element analysis is performed in every iteration, leading to the efficiency bottleneck especially when dense meshes are used to achieve high-resolution designs. To address this limitation, eCNNTO is proposed to build upon Kallioras et al. (2020), where a Deep Belief Network (DBN) was trained for every element to predict its near-optimal density from its early history, thereby skipping the great majority of iterations and significantly accelerating the TO procedure. However, the method lacks spatial correlations among neighboring elements and may lead to disconnected features in the final structure. The proposed method employs CNN with residual connections to address this issue. On top of it, a novel training strategy is introduced to further enhance the optimization efficiency, where the training dataset consists of the final stage density histories rather than early ones. This change can also help reduce the required training data size. eCNNTO requires only a small dataset to train and yet it can be generalized to problems with largely different boundary conditions, loading cases, design domain geometries, mesh resolutions, as well as non-design domains. In the end, the generalization capabilities and efficiency of eCNNTO are demonstrated through a variety of examples in two and three dimensions, achieving up to 90% and 97% reduction of iterations, respectively.
ai_explanation: 该论文用 CNN 加速基于有限元分析的拓扑优化，直接属于 AI 与计算力学/材料结构设计/科学计算交叉。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文提出 eCNNTO，一种 element-based 卷积神经网络，用于加速密度法拓扑优化。拓扑优化通常需要在每轮迭代中进行有限元分析，计算成本较高，尤其是在高分辨率网格下。作者用神经网络预测单元近优密度，以减少传统优化中的迭代和有限元计算负担。该研究是典型的 AI4Science/AI for engineering design，涉及深度学习、结构优化和计算力学。

title: Modularity-Free Conflict-Averse Training for Generalized PINNs
abstract: arXiv:2606.20156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have become a powerful framework for solving PDEs by embedding physical laws into differentiable objectives. Despite their advances, training PINNs remains fragile: recent conflict-averse optimization schemes alleviate gradient interference between residual and boundary losses, but we show that their effectiveness deteriorates as model capacity increases. In this paper, we identify a capacity-induced failure mode, where overparameterized networks undergo functional modularity, self-partitioning into task-exclusive modules that suppress cross-objective interaction and hinder convergence toward Pareto-stationary points. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework, Modular-Sparsity Synchronization (ModSync), which integrates structural optimization into conflict-averse training by penalizing task-exclusive connections while preserving interaction-promoting pathways. Extensive experiments across diverse PDE benchmarks demonstrate that ModSync consistently prevents capacity-driven failures, sustains robust cross-objective coupling, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy. Codes are available at r̆lhttps://github.com/heejokong/ModSync.
authors: Heejo Kong, Beomchul Park, Sung-Jin Kim, Seong-Whan Lee
ai_explanation: 该论文直接研究物理信息神经网络 PINNs 的训练问题，属于 AI 求解 PDE 和物理建模的典型 AI4Science 方向。
ai_detailed_summary: 研究对象是广义 PINNs 在求解偏微分方程时的训练稳定性问题。论文分析了大容量网络下残差损失与边界损失之间的梯度冲突及功能模块化失效现象。方法上提出或研究无模块化的冲突规避训练策略，以改善 PINN 的泛化和优化表现。该工作对利用神经网络求解物理方程和科学计算问题具有直接意义。

title: How LLMs Fail and Generalize in RTL Coding for Hardware Design?
abstract: arXiv:2606.19347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Translating sequential programming priors into the parallel temporal logic of hardware design remains a crucial bottleneck for large language models(LLM). To investigate this, we introduce a new error taxonomy grounded in problem solvability, inspired by cognitive theory. Our taxonomy categorizes failures into syntactic, semantic, solvable functional, and unsolvable functional types. Evaluations reveal a strict empirical ceiling on the VerilogEval benchmark, as frontier models plateau at a 90.8% initial pass rate. These plateaus are defined by unsolvable functional errors, exposing persistent knowledge gaps immune to test time compute scaling. Furthermore, we expose a striking surface convergence gap: optimization readily eliminates syntax errors but concurrently exacerbates deeper functional failures. Our findings demonstrate that alignment techniques merely teach models to compile. While repeated sampling strategies can patch solvable errors, register-transfer level(RTL) coding capacity remains strictly bounded by pretraining knowledge. Addressing challenges in the current LLM based hardware generation pipeline requires more studies in model reasoning rather than alignment interventions.
authors: Guan-Ting Liu, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Chenhui Deng, Zhongzhi Yu, Brucek Khailany, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang
ai_explanation: 该论文研究 LLM 在 RTL 硬件设计代码生成中的失败与泛化。虽然与芯片/硬件工程有关，但核心是代码生成与 EDA 自动化，不是物理、化学、材料或科学计算模拟。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文提出面向 VerilogEval 的错误分类体系，用于分析 LLM 将顺序编程先验迁移到并行时序硬件逻辑时的失败模式。作者将错误分为语法、语义、可解功能和不可解功能等类别，并观察到前沿模型存在初始通过率平台。研究揭示了 LLM 在硬件描述语言生成中的泛化边界。其与工程自动化相关，但未直接处理物理器件、材料或科学仿真问题。

title: DynAMO:Dynamic Asset Management Orchestration via Topological Multi-Agent Scheduling
abstract: arXiv:2606.19382v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While LLM-powered agents offer end-to-end automation for industrial asset lifecycles, real-world Industry 4.0 deployment is hindered by latency, concurrency instability, and safety risks. We present DynAMO (Dynamic Asset Management Orchestration), a deployment-ready engine using a Plan-then-Execute architecture to generate verifiable workflow graphs. DynAMO supports both SequentialWorkflow (topological execution) and ParallelWorkflow (dependency-aware concurrency). By dynamically identifying independent tasks, DynAMO preserves structural correctness and safety while significantly improving efficiency through controlled reasoning overlap. Across six controlled experiments on the AssetOpsBench industrial benchmark, DynAMO demonstrates substantial performance and robustness gains. Parallel execution reduces end-to-end latency by a median of 1.6x over sequential orchestration, rising to 1.8x on highly parallelizable workflows. After instrumenting external tool calls with realistic latencies, a latency decomposition shows that LLM reasoning and orchestration still account for more than 90% of execution time, identifying model inference as the primary system bottleneck. Structured context pruning reduces inference latency by approximately 30%, and DynAMO maintains correct functional behaviour (task completion, agent sequencing, and output quality) while exhibiting graceful degradation under controlled fault injection. Reproducibility analysis further confirms stable execution under repeated runs, with parallel scheduling reducing latency variance. These findings establish DynAMO as a practical blueprint for scalable, safe, and latency-aware agent deployment in Industry 4.0 automation pipelines. Code is available at: https://github.com/kushwaha001/DynAMO
authors: Kanishk Kushwaha, Vikrant Vinod Bansode, Harsh Vardhan, Dhaval C. Patel
ai_explanation: 该论文研究工业资产生命周期中的 LLM 多智能体调度和工作流编排。虽然提到 Industry 4.0，但核心是业务/工业流程自动化，不是材料、物理或科学计算发现。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文提出 DynAMO，用 Plan-then-Execute 架构生成可验证的工作流图，支持顺序和并行任务执行。系统通过识别独立任务来提高并发效率，同时控制延迟、稳定性和安全风险。应用对象是工业资产管理流程中的 LLM Agent 自动化。该研究不涉及科学实验数据建模、材料发现或物理化学模拟。

title: A Tool for the Synthesis of Adaptive Probabilistic Processors Based on the Ising Model
abstract: arXiv:2606.19533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work presents a tool for the synthesis and simulation of probabilistic architectures for solving combinatorial optimization problems by mapping them to the Ising model. The proposed approach automatically constructs the Ising Hamiltonian and determines the number of probabilistic elements (p-bits) based on problem characteristics such as size and topology. Furthermore, the tool introduces an adaptive strategy for selecting the most suitable update algorithm among Gibbs Sampling, Simulated Annealing (SA), Simulated Quantum Annealing (SQA), and cluster-based methods. Experimental results using benchmark problems demonstrate improved convergence behavior and flexibility compared to fixed approaches. The proposed framework enables systematic evaluation of probabilistic computing strategies and supports the development of future hardware implementations based on MTJs and p-bits.
authors: Jonathan Juracy Carneiro da Silva, Leonardo R. Gobatto, Jose Rodrigo Azambuja
ai_explanation: 该论文基于 Ising 模型构建概率计算架构，并涉及 Hamiltonian、Gibbs 采样、模拟退火和模拟量子退火。它属于物理启发计算与组合优化交叉方向，符合 AI×物理/计算科学范畴。
ai_detailed_summary: 论文提出一种用于合成和仿真概率处理器架构的工具，将组合优化问题映射到 Ising 模型。方法会自动构造 Ising Hamiltonian，并依据问题规模和拓扑确定 p-bit 等概率元件数量。系统还自适应选择 Gibbs Sampling、Simulated Annealing 和 Simulated Quantum Annealing 等更新算法。该工作体现了统计物理模型在计算优化硬件和算法设计中的应用。

title: Review of Machine Learning Models for Solar Energetic Particle Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2606.19539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) events have attracted increasing attention due to their significant radiation hazards for aviation, spacecraft electronics, and human missions beyond Earth's magnetosphere. From a scientific perspective, SEP events are intriguing because they arise from a set of physical processes extending from the solar surface and corona through the heliosphere, offering insight into particle acceleration and transport mechanisms that are widely applicable across astrophysics. Therefore, advancing our ability to understand and predict SEP events is essential both for deepening our knowledge of such mechanisms and for safeguarding space technologies and exploration. Traditionally, researchers have modeled SEPs using physics-based simulations and empirical methods. More recently, machine learning (ML) has emerged as a new tool for understanding and predicting SEP events. The purpose of this manuscript is to review the currently available ML models for SEP prediction, identify the datasets used for training, compare their architectures, inputs, and outputs, and, based on these insights, outline good practices and recommendations for future research.

title: Foreign Object Damage Mechanism of Ti60 Alloy under High-Temperature Conditions
abstract: To address the problem of foreign object damage (FOD) to titanium alloy compressor blades in aero-engines under high-temperature conditions, FOD tests under the same parameters at room temperature and 500℃ were conducted on Ti60 specimens. The macroscopic and microscopic characteristics of the foreign object damage were observed by scanning electron microscopy, energy dispersive spectroscopy and electron backscatter diffraction(EBSD). The research results show that high temperature has a significant impact on the foreign object damage behavior of Ti60 alloy. Under the same impact conditions, the specimens tested at 500℃ suffered much more severe damage than those tested at room temperature. The average crater depth, crater diameter and backside bulge height increased by 63.6%, 20.3% and 91.5%, respectively. High temperature also promoted surface oxidation, forming a brittle oxide layer that fractured under the impact load, causing the generation and propagation of cracks, and ultimately resulting in a network of cracks and continuous macroscopic fracture on the surface of the craters. In addition, high temperature changed the deformation response of Ti60 alloy at room temperature, transforming it from a relatively localized plastic deformation mode to a composite mode with more extensive plastic flow and more severe local deformation at the crater center.
ai_explanation: 该论文研究 Ti60 钛合金在高温条件下的外物损伤机制，属于金属材料与高温力学行为。材料表征和损伤机制研究与 AI×材料潜在应用高度相关。
ai_detailed_summary: 研究针对航空发动机压气机叶片用 Ti60 钛合金在高温下的外物损伤问题开展实验。作者比较室温和 500℃ 条件下相同冲击参数造成的损伤，并采用扫描电镜、能谱和 EBSD 分析微观组织变化。论文揭示高温对 Ti60 合金冲击损伤形貌和变形机制具有显著影响。该类材料损伤数据可用于机器学习寿命预测、微结构-性能关联建模和高温合金设计。

title: Spatial Distribution and Controlling Factors of Vanadium and Chromium in a Vanadium- Titanium Magnetite Tailings Reservoir and Surrounding Soils in the Panxi Region
abstract: Vanadium (V) and chromium (Cr) in soils surrounding vanadium-titanium magnetite tailings reservoirs represent important environmental risks, especially after reservoir closure and soil covering. This study investigated a closed, soil-covered tailings reservoir in the Panxi region using surface soils and S-series vertical profiles. ArcGIS interpolation, BCR sequential extraction, Visual MINTEQ scenario simulation and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-SHAP modeling were combined to characterize spatial distribution, chemical fractionation, potential aqueous speciation and controlling factors. V and Cr concentrations ranged from 25.87 to 621.05 and from 13.03 to 385.07 mg kg− 1, with maxima 4.53 and 4.62 times regional background values, respectively. V enrichment was relatively widespread, whereas Cr enrichment was more localized. Hotspots occurred mainly near the dam toe and in sedimentary zones, indicating coupled effects of tailings input, runoff transport and local deposition. Vertical profiles showed profile-specific enrichment without consistent depth trends. Sequential extraction indicated that V and Cr were mainly residual, suggesting limited short-term mobility, although non-residual fractions still indicated potential release risks. Under an oxidized Visual MINTEQ scenario, V(V) was predicted mainly as H2VO4−, whereas Cr(VI) was mainly CaCrO4(aq). Correlation and LightGBM-SHAP analyses identified amorphous Fe/Al, exchangeable Ca/Mg, pH, CEC, SOM, texture and dam-toe proximity as major controls. Overall, V and Cr contamination around the closed and soil-covered tailings reservoir was controlled by coupled processes of tailings input, runoff transport, mineral fixation and soil physicochemical regulation. Future risk assessments should focus on dam-toe sedimentary zones and integrate total concentrations, chemical fractions, landform conditions and machine-learning results.

title: Nd-Doped NiFe₂O₄ Nanoparticles for Enhanced X-Band Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
abstract: Doping rare-earth (RE) elements into ferrites is an effective strategy for modifying their physical structure, magnetic response, and electromagnetic-wave absorption behavior. In this study, nickel ferrite nanoparticles were modified with a small amount of neodymium (Nd) using a simple coprecipitation method. The influence of Nd content on morphology, crystal structure, elemental composition, magnetic properties, and X-band absorption performance was investigated using SEM-EDX, XRD, EDX mapping, VSM, and vector-network-analyzer measurements. The results confirmed the successful formation of Nd-doped nickel ferrite materials with different Nd contents. Nd incorporation reduced nanoparticle agglomeration and altered the magnetic parameters, particularly saturation magnetization and coercive field, thereby improving impedance matching and electromagnetic-wave attenuation in the 8–12 GHz range. The strongest reflection loss reached − 25.47 dB at 11.56 GHz for the NiFe₁.₉₇Nd₀.₀₃O₄ sample at a matching thickness of 2.0 mm, corresponding to an electromagnetic-wave absorption efficiency of approximately 99.7%. These results indicate that Nd-doped NiFe₂O₄ nanoparticles are promising candidates for X-band electromagnetic-wave absorption and shielding applications.

title: Facile Co-Precipitation Synthesis of Spinel CoFe3O4 Nanoparticles with Enhanced Visible-Light Photocatalytic and Antimicrobial Performance
abstract: The structural, optical, morphological, photocatalytic, antibacterial, and antifungal properties of CoFe3O4 nanoparticles were thoroughly examined after they were successfully synthesized using a simple co-precipitation method. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman spectroscopy, and UV-visible spectroscopy were used to characterize the produced nanoparticles. With an optical band gap of 1.55 eV and strong visible-light absorption, UV-Vis analysis demonstrated exceptional visible-light responsiveness. Phase-pure spinel CoFe3O4 with good crystallinity and suitable oxidation states was confirmed by Raman, XRD, and XPS investigations. Analyses using FE-SEM and EDS showed homogeneous elemental distribution and almost spherical morphology. Due to improved charge separation and reactive oxygen species production, the nanoparticles demonstrated effective visible light-driven photocatalytic activity. Significant antifungal and antibacterial effects against a variety of pathogenic microbes were also noted. These results demonstrate the potential of CoFe3O4 nanoparticles as multipurpose nanomaterials for antimicrobial and environmental remediation applications.

title: Depth-dependent coupling of dissolved organic matter chemodiversity and microbial community traits reveals threshold effects of combined fertilization on soil carbon stabilization in arid agroecosystems
abstract: Background How fertilization influences the coupled dynamics of DOM composition and microbial communities across soil depths in arid agroecosystems remains unclear.Methods The molecular composition of DOM and microbial communities in surface (0–20 cm) and subsurface (20–40 cm) soil layers from a 7-year field experiment comprising six fertilization treatments: no fertilization (CK), chemical fertilizer (NPK), organic fertilizer (M), half-rate chemical fertilizer plus M (0.5NPKM), chemical fertilizer plus M (NPKM), and 1.5-fold chemical fertilizer plus M (1.5NPKM) was analysied using spectroscopic, mass spectrometric, and sequencing approaches.Results NPK and M treatments significantly reduced DOM content in the surface layer by 12.14% and 22.87%, respectively, relative to CK. However, combined fertilization increased surface DOM content compared with the single treatments, and this effect became more pronounced with higher proportions of NPK. Organic fertilizer enhanced DOM aromaticity and facilitated the transformation of humic-like into protein-like and fulvic-like components. The application of organic fertilizer promoted the conversion of oxygen-rich and labile compounds (aliphatic/peptide-like and lipids) into nitrogen- and sulfur-containing compounds as well as more aromatic structures. Combined organic-inorganic fertilization enriched Proteobacteria/Ascomycota and increased microbial network complexity. Actinobacteria consumed labile substrates, while Acidobacteria/Chloroflexi allowed persistence via slow utilization. Fungi driving both the synthesis of fresh microbial metabolites in surface soils and the formation of stable carbon pools in subsurface layers through humification and lipid accumulation. Ascomycota regulating DOM aromaticity in the surface layer and coupling with nitrogen cycling in the subsurface.Conclusion Organic-inorganic fertilization drives soil organic carbon stabilization through molecular-level DOM-microbe interactions.

title: Microemulsion-Assisted Formation of P3P6T: PCBM Bulk Heterojunctions via Ultrasonic Spray Deposition for application in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Aqueous-processable conjugated polymers offer an environment-friendly pathway for organic solar cell fabrication. In this work, a bulk-heterojunction(BHJ) comprising water soluble poly(3-(potassium-6-hexanoate) thiophene-2,5-diyl) (P3P6T) as donor and(6,6(-phenyl-C-61-butyric acid methyl ester)) (PCBM) as acceptor was synthesized using a microemulsion approach in combination with ultrasonic spray deposition. Two orthogonal solvents, water for P3P6T and dichlorobenzene for PCBM were used. These were mixed with isopropanol in specific proportions, to form a stable microemulsion. Use of orthogonal solvents for the donor and acceptor enabled controlled separation of donor–acceptor pure phases during spray deposition. Morphological and optical studies revealed that as-deposited films exhibited submicron sized PCBM islands. Short-time thermal annealing (120 °C, 5 min) promoted interfacial diffusion and the formation of continuous interpenetrating donor–acceptor networks, as evidenced by red-shifted absorption and strong photoluminescence quenching. Prolonged annealing led to over-coarsening and reduced interfacial areas. The optimized device, with structure ITO/PEDOT:PSS/P3HT/P3P6T:PCBM/ PCBM /Al, achieved a power conversion efficiency of 2.56% with Voc = 0.56 V, Jsc = 11.31 mA cm⁻², and FF = 40.4%. The study demonstrates that microemulsion-assisted ultrasonic spray deposition enables morphology control in aqueous-processable BHJ systems and provides a scalable route for environmentally friendly OPV fabrication. Relevance Summary: This work is focused on a novel microemulsion-assisted ultrasonic spray approach, which uses orthogonal solvents and a co-solvent to precisely control donor–acceptor morphology in aqueous-processable BHJ systems. Unlike prior studies, it allows tunable, pure and optimized submicron scale phase separation, which is an essential factor for BHJ based optoelectronic devices. This work advances scalable, eco-friendly fabrication of organic solar cells with enhanced morphology control.

title: Synergistic Experimental and Quantum Chemical Investigation of Heavy Metal Immobilization in Industrial Soils
abstract: Industrial discharge from the textile and dyeing industries in Tamil Nadu’s Tiruppur district has severely contaminated the soil with heavy metals, posing significant ecological and human health risks. This study assesses vermicomposting as a sustainable and eco-friendly bioremediation strategy for detoxifying these heavy metal-contaminated soils. Industrially polluted soil samples were subjected to vermicomposting using Eisenia fetida with organic amendments such as cattle dung and decomposed plant residues under controlled conditions for 45–60 days. Changes in soil properties and heavy metal concentrations were measured before and after treatment using Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (AAS). The results showed a substantial reduction in all analysed heavy metals with cadmium removal being the most effective (0.9516 to 0.1355 ppm) followed by chromium (0.2980 to 0.0773 ppm), nickel (0.6855 to 0.4218 ppm) and lead (0.5423 to 0.3128 ppm). To understand the molecular mechanisms behind metal immobilisation Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations and Molecular Electrostatic Potential (MEP) analysis were used to examine interactions between heavy metals and vermicompost-derived humic substances. DFT results indicated favourable binding energies and reduced HOMO-LUMO energy gaps confirming the high affinity of carboxyl, hydroxyl and phenolic groups for metal ions. MEP mapping revealed electron-rich regions as dominant metal-binding sites supporting strong adsorption and complexation. The combined experimental and computational findings suggest metal reduction occurs through synergistic mechanisms involving earthworm bioaccumulation, microbial-mediated redox transformations, humification and stable metal-organic complex formation. Crucially, the microbial reduction of toxic hexavalent chromium to the less mobile trivalent form was key to chromium detoxification. Beyond metal stabilisation, vermicomposting significantly increased soil organic carbon, nutrient availability (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium) and microbial activity. This indicates effective soil health restoration. The final metal concentrations were well below internationally accepted permissible limits for agricultural soils. Overall, this study demonstrates that Eisenia fetida-based vermicomposting, supported by DFT and MEP insights, is a cost-effective low-energy and environmentally safe strategy for remediating and sustainably managing heavy metal-contaminated industrial soils.

title: Global utility-scale photovoltaics are structurally displaced from electricity demand centres
abstract: The system value of solar photovoltaics (PV) increasingly depends on effectively connecting generation to electricity demand. Here, we develop an integrated framework to diagnose this spatial constraint globally. Using Sentinel-2 imagery and deep learning, we map near-global utility-scale PV plants at 10-m resolution for 2025. Coupling this with generation models and a 1-km nighttime-light-derived electricity demand surface, we estimate ~ 1,852 TWh of annual PV generation against ~ 32.8 PWh of demand, yielding a ~ 5.65% mean penetration. Structural under-coverage is widespread: ~82% and 91% of global electricity demand lie in provinces below the 8.6% and 15.7% IEA reference thresholds, respectively. Under IEA-aligned scenarios requiring ~ 3,990 and ~ 5,910 TWh of PV supply, meeting demand relies heavily on domestic redistribution (~ 77.5%). Transfers exhibit a clear distance hierarchy, with > 80% occurring within 1,500 km and mean connection distances of ~ 593–718 km. This reveals dual infrastructure needs: expanding regional backbone networks and developing high-capacity long-distance corridors. As targets rise, the bottleneck shifts from reallocating existing production to mobilizing new potential via transmission and flexibility. We conclude the limiting factor is spatial system integration, requiring corridor-aware planning for equitable decarbonization.

title: Energy-Exchange Driven Effective Field Framework (EE-DEFF): A Reproducible Variational Stochastic Model of Emergent Structures
abstract: We propose a variational stochastic effective field framework describing emergent structures in non-equilibrium energy-exchange systems. The model introduces a continuous scalar field Φ(x,t) governed by structural relaxation, energy-gradient coupling, and stochastic fluctuations. Grounded in the fundamental premise that physical configuration states manifest through localized absorption and emission dynamics, we demonstrate that stable particle-like structures correspond to metastable extrema of an effective action functional. Incorporating numerical validation under explicit bounds, the proposed framework shows significantly enhanced convergence stability and scaling performance over classical stochastic baselines. In the diffusion limit, the model maintains mathematical consistency with stochastic formulations of quantum mechanics. The framework serves as a reproducible interpretive effective theory and establishes testable phenomenological directions via energy fluctuation scaling in high-energy regimes.

title: Responses of the macroalgae Ulva lactuca (Ulvales, Chlorophyta) and Sargassum cymosum (Fucales, Ochrophyta) to thermal stress evaluated by PAM fluorometry
abstract: There is growing concern regarding the thermal effects of global warming on benthic marine macroalgae, which are ecologically important ecosystem engineers on rocky shores. Metabolic responses to thermal stress vary among species and depend on their optimal temperature and tolerance range. Physiological studies using pulse amplitude modulated (PAM) fluorometry to assess photosystem II are essential for understanding macroalgal responses to temperature fluctuations. This study evaluated photosystem II response behavior under extreme temperature conditions in Ulva lactuca Linnaeus and Sargassum cymosum C. Agardh to detect the sensitivity of these species to temperature variation. Maximum and effective quantum efficiencies (Fv/Fm and ΔF/Fm′) and photosystem II thermal tolerance were measured under 25°C (control) and 35°C (thermal stress) conditions in the laboratory. Both species showed reduced Fv/Fm and ΔF/Fm′ values at 35°C, with Ulva lactuca being the most affected species. The thermal stability of photosystem II was not altered between the tested temperatures but was consistently lower in Sargassum cymosum. These results indicate that thermal stress resistance and exposure frequency in their natural habitats influence species-specific thermal tolerance. Ulva lactuca, which is typical of intertidal zones with frequent short-term thermal fluctuations, loses its photosystem II efficiency and biomass under prolonged thermal stress. In contrast, Sargassum cymosum, found in warm subtidal waters, exhibits greater tolerance and maintains growth despite its reduced photosystem II efficiency. Thus, photosystem II thermal stability and photosynthetic efficiency appeared to be independently selected.

title: A Local Ontological Model of Double-Slit Fringes via Moiré Sampling and Non-Linear Detection
abstract: Feynman’s classic exposition of the double-slit experiment asserts that no local, particle-only ontology can reproduce quantum interference fringes without invoking wave-particle duality or nonlocal communication. We re-examine the implicit assumptions of this paradigm by constructing a strictly local, counterfactual-definite sampling model. The framework relies on four components: (i) an oscillating detector substrate that modulates single-particle detection efficiency; (ii) a geometric moir´e (beat) pattern emerging from independent slit trajectories; (iii) a finite detector relaxation memory that provides a non-linear readout; and (iv) source-detector phase coherence. We demonstrate that while linear averaging over the sub-wavelength carrier landscape washes out the signal (the “Addition Problem”), a non-linear detector memory successfully extracts the macroscopic quantum envelope, yielding an r ≈ 0.89 Pearson correlation with the Born-rule intensity profile in Monte Carlo simulations across multiple detection functions. This work isolates the passivedetection assumption as a critical, unstated premise in traditional quantum impossibility arguments and provides an operational, local-causal alternative for single-particle interference statistics.

title: A magnetic environment with reproducible spatio-temporal magnetic conditions at picotesla level
abstract: Walk-in, picotesla-scale environments are essential for measurements of biomagnetism and fundamental physics. However, conventional rooms require typical active dynamic compensation, which adds complexity and magnetic noise. Here, we present a solution that achieves an absolute residual field well below 100pT within its central measurement volume. Following magnetic equilibration, this environment achieves picotesla-scale reproducibility. Consequently, optically pumped magnetometers operate at their design noise and drift performance and remain operational during sensor motion without active feedback. A key technique is robotic mapping, which resolves the ultra-low residual field patterns and demagnetization stability. We demonstrate the platform's versatility through high-fidelity adult and fetal magnetocardiography, standing magnetoencephalography, and ultra-low field magnetic resonance with polarized noble gases in the limit of strongly coupled spins in a negligible holding field. The achieved passive reproducibility turns the ultra-low magnetic background into a predictable, correctable property, establishing a novel foundation for next-generation quantum sensing and precision physics.

title: Investigating quantum and molecular plumbing in nanofluidics research
abstract: Our body contains an intricate system of tiny vessels through which blood, water and other molecules flow. title: PI-SONet: A Physics-Informed Symplectic Operator Network for Real-Time Optimal Control of Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Many real-life applications involve controlling high-dimensional multi-agent systems in real-time. Existing optimal control solvers often suffer from the curse-of-dimensionality and require complete rerunning for each new problem setting. We target nonconvex, nonlinear problems in 100s of dimensions by introducing PI-SONet (Physics-Informed Symplectic Operator Network), a structure-preserving operator learning framework for solving parameterized families of optimal control problems and their Pontraygin Maximum Principle (PMP) systems. PI-SONet combines a latent right-space solver with a conditional symplectic operator to produce tractable Hamiltonian trajectories in a computationally efficient auxiliary space and transform them back to physical space. This decomposition yields a single trained operator that approximates the PMP solution map, inherently preserves Hamiltonian structure, and generalizes across unseen problem configurations. Unlike existing methods, which are fundamentally single-instance solvers, PI-SONet achieves sub-second inferences on new problem instances, equating to up to 10,000x speedup over representative baselines. These results suggest that structure-preserving neural operators provide a practical route toward reusable, real-time surrogates for high-dimensional optimal control.

title: Synergy of Surface Oxygen Vacancies and Built-in Electric Field in 0D/2D CeO2/SnSe2 S-scheme Heterojunctions for Enhanced Photocatalytic Malachite Green Degradation
abstract: Industrial effluents exacerbate aqueous contamination, necessitating the urgent remediation of toxic dyes such as Malachite Green (MG). In this study, a 0D/2D S-scheme heterojunction was constructed by anchoring CeO2 nanocubes onto SnSe2 hexagonal nanosheets via a precisely controlled two-step hydrothermal strategy. In-situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis corroborates that illumination triggers the proliferation of surface oxygen vacancies. These photo-induced oxygen vacancies (Ov) empower the CeO2/SnSe2 heterostructure to sustain exceptional catalytic activity over five consecutive cycles. Moreover, the optimized 0.2 g CeO2/SnSe2 composite exhibits a remarkable degradation efficiency of over 98% for MG within 30 minutes. Such performance enhancement is attributed by the synergy between the 0D/2D dimensional matching and a potent internal electric field (IEF), which triggers an S-scheme charge transfer mechanism to preserve high redox potential while accelerating carrier separation. This work provides a sophisticated blueprint for designing dimension-matched S-scheme heterojunctions for high-performance environmental remediation.

title: Dip Angle–Viscosity–Rate Coupling Controls Fracture Complexity and Pressure/AE Fingerprints in Steeply Dipping Coal: Evidence from 2 m-Scale True-Triaxial Hydraulic Fracturing Experiments
abstract: Steeply dipping coal reservoirs exhibit strong structural anisotropy controlled by bedding/cleat systems, which promotes fracture deflection, branching, and network connectivity changes that complicate hydraulic fracturing design. This paper presents a focused subset of results from 2 m-scale true-triaxial hydraulic fracturing experiments, emphasizing the coupled influence of dip angle, fluid viscosity, and injection rate on fracture complexity and pressure–acoustic emission (AE) fingerprints. Large specimens (2 m × 2 m × 1 m) were fractured using active water (µ = 3 mPa·s) and a viscosified emulsion (µ = 20 mPa·s). Fracture traces were mapped on split surfaces and quantified by fractal dimension, while injection pressure and AE/microseismic event activity were recorded. Under low-rate injection (Q = 0.1 m³/min), fracture complexity shows clear dip-dependent viscosity sensitivity with fractal dimensions of D = 1.731 (active water, 45°), 1.693 (active water, 70°), 1.685 (emulsion, 45°), and 1.757 (emulsion, 70°). Pressure–AE curves further show that active water tends to produce sharper breakdown-and-decline signatures, whereas the viscosified emulsion generates plateau-like multi-peak oscillations, consistent with intermittent propagation, temporary restriction/bridging, and re-opening cycles reported in hydraulic fracture theory and diagnostics. At high dip (70°), increasing rate from 0.4 to 0.5 m³/min shifts the response from relatively stable opening to persistent multi-peak oscillatory behavior with episodic event bursts—an operational fingerprint indicative of complex fracture generation. These findings provide an engineering basis to balance stimulated reservoir volume (SRV) potential against controllability in steeply dipping coal by selecting appropriate viscosity–rate windows.

title: Electrospinning Preparation of TiO2 Fiber Membranes and the Enhancement of Photocatalytic Uranium Reduction Efficiency by One-Dimensional Morphology
abstract: Nuclear energy as a key low-carbon, sustainable, and clean energy source, it's proportion in the global energy structure continues to increase. However, the rapid development of nuclear energy inevitably leads to the generation of a large amount of uranium-containing wastewater, posing serious risks to environment and health. Uranium in aqueous systems predominantly exists in the form of mobile and toxic U(VI) (UO22⁺), while U(IV) has very low solubility in water and is easier to remove. Photocatalytic reduction of highly soluble U(VI) to sparingly soluble U(IV) offers a promising route for uranium recovery. However, conventional photocatalysts with typically powder material that suffer from low activity, aggregation, and poor recyclability. Therefore, we developed a TiO2 fiber membranes with a high aspect ratio, self-supporting, and non-agglomerating, demonstrating excellent performance in photocatalytic reduction of U(VI). The experimental results indicated that 400°C was the optimal heat treatment temperature, and the TiO2 fiber membranes heat-treated at this temperature exhibited the highest photocatalytic reduction efficiency. At pH 5, the membranes achieved 99.0% uranium removal within 180 minutes without sacrificial agents, which 2.47 times higher than commercial Anatase TiO2 powder. Moreover, the TiO2 membranes still demonstrates a high removal efficiency for U(VI) after five reacting cycles. In photoluminescence spectroscopy, the emission intensity of TiO2 fiber films was significantly reduced compared to that of Anatase TiO2 powder, indicating effective suppression of the recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. This was attributed to its one-dimensional structure, which provides a continuous path for charge transport, thereby minimizing charge recombination and enhancing reaction efficiency.

title: Pathways to Net Zero: Evaluating Saf, Hydrogen and Dual-Fuel Propulsion for Next-Generation Derivative Regional Aircraft
abstract: While passenger numbers in air travel are projected to continue increasing, the aviation industry has set the goal to reach net zero CO2 emissions by 2050. In this paper, alternative energy carriers such as SAF, hydrogen and batteries are analysed in regard to their suitability to decarbonize regional aviation. The analysis is conducted based on the D328eco and potential derivatives: a hydrogen-burn concept, a hydrogen-fuel cell concept, a dual-fuel concept able to burn kerosene as well as hydrogen, and a battery-electric concept. The derivatives are designed for a range of 600 NM, covering a sufficient share of the regional route network. It is shown that SAF is the only near-term solution and that it will still be required after the introduction of hydrogen aircraft for airport pairs beyond the assumed design mission. The second promising concept to enable the usage of low-carbon hydrogen in aviation is the dual-fuel, exhibiting a high load-factor while enabling operations from and to airports with and without hydrogen infrastructure. Although being penalized in payload capability, the hydrogen-burn and fuel-cell concepts still have the potential to decarbonize regional aviation. It is demonstrated that the fuel-cell concept is contingent upon significant improvements in fuel cell technology and the electric powertrain. The battery-electric concept is not feasible in the foreseeable future.

title: MSTR-PPO: A Multi-Scale Temporal Residual PPO Controller for Freeze-Prone Indoor Navigation
abstract: Local navigation controllers can fail to make progress in constrained indoor environments when narrow geometry and moving obstacles compress the feasible local motion space. These freeze events trigger repeated recovery behaviors and can prevent otherwise valid global paths from being executed. This paper treats freezing as a failure of local control under three observable mechanisms: insufficient path horizon, motion ambiguity in single-frame sensing, and unstable learned velocity commands. We present MSTR-PPO (Multi-Scale Temporal Residual Proximal Policy Optimization), a freeze-aware residual local controller defined at the standard sensor--path--velocity-command interface. Rather than replacing the geometric controller with an unconstrained end-to-end policy, MSTR-PPO learns a bounded correction around a Pure Pursuit nominal action. The controller uses a Multi-Scale Path Transformer for near-, mid-, and far-horizon route context, a First-Order Temporal High-Pass Filter for low-cost light detection and ranging (LiDAR) range-change cues, and a Bounded Residual Action around Pure Pursuit. We evaluate eight local-control variants across nine Gazebo worlds with dynamic obstacles, totaling 2,880 trials across all methods, and deploy the trained policy through a Robot Operating System 2 (ROS, 2) Navigation 2 (Nav2) C++ controller interface as a representative evaluation stack. In the two target freeze-prone worlds, MSTR-PPO reaches the goal in all 80 evaluated trials and triggers no stack-level recovery events, while the best default-parameter classical baseline reaches 86.2% success on the same subset. On the main seven-world evaluation suite (W1--W7), MSTR-PPO obtains 91.1% average success and runs with 5--10, ms central processing unit (CPU) control-cycle latency. Stress tests expose a limitation on continuous-curvature paths, and a preliminary Unitree Go2 test succeeds in 27 of 30 trials.

title: Photophysical Insights of Blue–Green Emitting Oxadiazole: Efficient Energy Transfer in Core–Shell Quantum Dot Hybrids
abstract: The development of blue–green emitting organic chromophores with excellent optoelectronic properties remains an important issue. In this context, the synthesis of a novel blue–green emitting chromophore, 2-(4-(2-(anthracen-10-yl)vinyl)phenyl)-5-(4-tert-butylphenyl)-1,3,4-oxadiazole (AVBO), was accomplished via the donor–π–acceptor (D- π–A) strategy using a Wittig reaction. The integration of aryl-heteroaryl groups and the oxadiazole group was utilized to obtain efficient blue–green emission with excellent optical properties. AVBO exhibited stable and efficient PL in the range of 485–510 nm across diverse solvent environments. Solvatochromic analysis using multiple correlations (Lippert-Mataga, Bakhshiev, Kawski-Chamma-Viallet, and Reichardt) revealed a significantly higher excited-state dipole moment compared to the ground state (μₑ>μ_g), with a parallel orientation (φ=0⁰⁾. The values calculated using these empirical equations were compared with those calculated computationally. Kamlet-Taft and Catalán MLR analyses further identified dominant non-specific solvent interactions (π^*) alongside specific hydrogen-bonding donor contributions. To explore its potential in optoelectronic applications, AVBO was integrated into hybrid systems with ZnSe/ZnS core-shell quantum dots (7–8 nm). This assembly functioned as a efficient FRET mechanism, reaching an efficiency of 88% with Förster radii of 6.14–6.16 nm. The quenching kinetics, validated by Stern-Volmer plots, showed both static and dynamic components with super-diffusion-limited rate constants (kq  1014 /MS). Time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) confirmed energy transfer via dipole-dipole interactions. These findings highlight the AVBO-QDs hybrid as a promising, heavy-metal-free, and tunable emitter for light harvesting, photosensitization, and biosensing applications.

ai_detailed_summary: 研究合成了一种蓝绿色发光的 oxadiazole 类有机色团 AVBO，并考察其光致发光和光学稳定性。方法包括有机合成、供体-π-受体分子设计、光谱表征以及与核壳量子点杂化后的能量转移分析。主要发现是该分子在蓝绿色区域具有较好发光性能，并可在量子点杂化体系中表现出有效能量转移。该工作与发光材料、光电材料和纳米杂化体系设计密切相关，可为数据驱动发光材料筛选提供基础。

title: Influence of Cerium Oxide on the Structural, Optical, and Luminescent Properties of Borophosphate Glasses
abstract: A glass series based on the borophosphate system was prepared with varying additions of CeO2 (57.5–x)B2O3–15P2O5–20Na2O–7.5CaO–xCeO2 (x = 0.3–0.9 mol%). Density and molar volume show non-linear behavior across all samples, reflecting structural rearrangements induced by rare-earth ions. The incorporation of CeO2 generally leads to structural modifications. Structural parameters such as internuclear distances and boron concentration also vary, indicating changes in the glass network connectivity. X-ray diffraction confirms the amorphous nature of all samples. FTIR analysis reveals the presence of structural units including BO3, BO4, P–O–P linkages, and hydroxyl-related groups. Optical studies indicate that the indirect band gap decreases with increasing CeO2 content. Urbach energy exhibits irregular variation, suggesting changes in structural disorder. The refractive index and electronic polarizability show composition-dependent trends, with CeO2 enhancing polarizability. A red shift in the absorption edge is observed with increasing cerium content. Photoluminescence spectra reveal an excitation around 290 nm corresponding to 4f–5d transitions of Ce3+ ions. Emission characteristics are strongly influenced by both CeO2 concentration, with observed transition at 373 nm corresponds to 5D5/2 to 2F7/2 attributed to phonon-assisted relaxation and radiative recombination. The obtained structural and optical properties suggest that these glass compositions are promising candidates for future bioactivity applications.

title: Decrease of magnetocaloric effect and magnetic susceptibility of ferromagnet due to magnetostructural phase transition
abstract: A theoretical model based on spin-exchange energy and the entropy of the magnetic subsystem provides a general framework for describing the temperature dependence of magnetization in systems undergoing magnetostructural phase transitions. By fitting the model to experimental magnetization curves, the key physical parameters governing these transitions are extracted. These parameters are used to calculate the magnetic-field-induced temperature change and magnetic susceptibility, including the paraprocess contribution. It is shown that, although magnetostructural transitions lead to a sharp change in magnetization, this alone is not sufficient to produce a giant magnetocaloric effect. Instead, the effect is strongly influenced by the magnetic susceptibility and the specific heat. The latter exhibits pronounced peaks in the presence of structural transitions, thereby reducing the adiabatic temperature change. The results demonstrate that large magnetization changes near first-order transitions do not guarantee strong magnetocaloric performance, in agreement with experimental observations for Ni-Mn-Ga-Cu alloys. The theory shows that materials exhibiting large peak values of magnetic susceptibility are the most promising for achieving a large magnetocaloric effect.

title: Piezoelectric manipulation and stacking-dependent magnetism in ferrovalley materials
abstract: The electronic transport characteristics of two-dimensional (2D) systems have widespread application prospects in the fabrication of multifunctional nanodevices. However, the current research for basic transport phenomena, such as anomalous valley Hall effect (AVHE) and piezoelectric response, is limited to discrete discussion. Here, we theoretically propose a valley-piezoelectricity coupling strategy beyond the existing paradigm to realize AVHE and layer Hall effect (LHE) in ferrovalley (FV) systems, and its essential principle can be extended to general valleytronic materials. Through first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that the large polarized electric field of 2.8×106 (1.67×107) V/m can be induced by 0.1% uniaxial strain in FV 2H-LaHF (1T-LaHF) monolayers. In addition, the microscopic mechanism of interlayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) state of 2H-LaHF bilayer is uncovered by the spin Hamiltonian and super-superexchange (SSE) interaction. Our findings pave the way for new explorations of valley Hall-related effect involving piezoelectricity.

title: Integrated Experimental-Machine Learning Framework for the Synthesis Optimization and Predictive Modeling of Iron Oxide Nanoparticles in Dye Removal Applications
abstract: This study presents an integrated experimental and machine learning framework for optimizing the co-precipitation synthesis of iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) and predicting their crystal size and specific surface area. A comparative evaluation of two precipitating agents showed that ammonium hydroxide produced superior results, yielding smaller crystal size (86 Å) and higher surface area (87.23 m²/g). A central composite experimental design was applied to model the effects of temperature (30-90 °C), stirring speed (100-600 rpm), and synthesis time (15-75 min) using Response Surface Methodology (RSM). The resulting models achieved high predictive performance, with R² values of 93.94% for crystal size and 92.40% for surface area. To improve model generalization, the dataset was expanded from 15 to 44 samples using Gaussian noise addition and linear interpolation. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regressors trained on the augmented data showed strong predictive ability, with test RMSE values of 10.47 Å (R² = 0.749) for crystal size and 0.91 m²/g (R² = 0.587) for surface area. Compared to RSM, XGBoost demonstrated superior accuracy and robustness. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining experimental design, data augmentation, and machine learning to optimize nanoparticle synthesis for environmental applications such as dye removal.

title: Stability of digital and analog quantum simulations under noise
abstract: Quantum simulation is a central application of near-term quantum devices, pursued in both analog and digital architectures. A key challenge for both paradigms is the effect of imperfections and noise on predictive power. In this work, we present a rigorous and physically transparent comparison of the stability of digital and analog quantum simulators under a variety of perturbative noise models. We provide rigorous worst- and average-case error bounds for noisy quantum simulation of local observables. We find that the two paradigms show comparable scaling in the worst case, while exhibiting different forms of enhanced error cancellation on average. We further analyze Gaussian and Brownian noise processes, deriving concentration bounds that capture typical deviations beyond worst-case guarantees. These results provide a unified framework for quantifying the robustness of noisy quantum simulations and identify regimes where digital methods have intrinsic advantages and when we can see similar behavior.

title: Interfacial control of orbital occupancy and spin state in LaCoO₃
abstract: Author(s): Ellen M. Kiens, Nicolas Gauquelin, Arno Annys, Emma van der Minne, Iris C. G. van den Bosch, Matthijs A. van Spronsen, Zezhong Zhang, Annick De Backer, Sandra Van Aert, Jo Verbeeck, Gertjan Koster, Bastian Mei, Frank M. F. de Groot, and Christoph Baeumer Interfacial engineering offers a powerful route to control electronic states in correlated oxides. Here, the authors demonstrate tunable Co 3 d orbital occupancy in LaCoO 3 heterostructures, spanning partial d 5 to d 7 configurations via tailored interfaces with LaTiO₃, LaMnO₃, LaNiO₃, and LaAlO₃. Combining X-ray absorption spectroscopy with multiplet calculations reveals interface-dependent charge transfer and spin-state modulation, while atomic-scale microscopy links these effects to strain and structural distortions. Notably, inserting a LaAlO₃ spacer suppresses charge transfer, stabilizing an unexpected low-spin d 6 state. These findings highlight how interfacial design governs orbital occupation and spin, providing a versatile platform for tuning functionality in oxide electronics and catalysis. [Phys. Rev. Materials 10, 066003] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026
authors: Ellen M. Kiens, Nicolas Gauquelin, Arno Annys, Emma van der Minne, Iris C. G. van den Bosch, Matthijs A. van Spronsen, Zezhong Zhang, Annick De Backer, Sandra Van Aert, Jo Verbeeck, Gertjan Koster, Bastian Mei, Frank M. F. de Groot, and Christoph Baeumer

title: A Statistical Time-Series Forecasting Approach to Coronal Mass Ejection Occurrence Rates Using ARIMA and ARIMAX Models
abstract: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are among the most energetic solar phenomena, and their occurrence rate is modulated by the solar magnetic cycle on timescales relevant to space weather forecasting. We present a statistical time-series forecasting framework based on ARIMA and ARIMAX models applied to five CME subpopulations drawn from the SOHO/LASCO CDAW catalog (January 1996 – November 2025, Solar Cycles 23–25), with the sunspot number as the exogenous predictor, evaluated through rigorous out-of-sample testing across a solar cycle transition. Purely autoregressive ARIMA/SARIMA models systematically fail to generalize beyond the training window, yielding negative out-of-sample R² in the majority of configurations. Incorporating the sunspot number as an exogenous regressor resolves this deficiency: at annual resolution, and under a nowcasting configuration in which observed sunspot numbers are used contemporaneously, R² reaches 0.87 and 0.83 for the entire and Moderate Partial Halo subpopulations, with RMSE reductions exceeding 60% in the best cases. Monthly models show consistent but more modest improvements (R² łeq 0.43), reflecting stochastic short-term variability not captured by the linear framework. Additionally, a purely prospective forecast of fast CME occurrence rates beyond the observed record is provided, independent of any nowcasting configuration, extending the predictive horizon of the framework toward Solar Cycle 25 decline and Solar Cycle 26.

title: A Data-Driven Actuarial Framework Integrating Statistical Modeling and Simulation for Solvency and Risk Assessment in Public Disability Insurance
abstract: Public disability insurance systems are becoming increasingly unpredictable as claim patterns, benefit growth, and labor market conditions change. The study creates a uniform, data-driven actuarial approach for determining the long-term solvency of a major public disability insurance scheme. Claim frequency, severity, and duration are analyzed with generalized linear models and time-series approaches, and their combined effects on fund sustainability are assessed using Monte Carlo simulation and stress testing. The paradigm accounts for overdispersion, temporal dependence, and stochastic interactions, resulting in probabilistic estimates of fund balances, ruin probabilities, and tail risk under both baseline and stressed circumstances. When applied to a multi-decade administrative dataset, the results suggest significant systemic risk, emphasizing the fund's vulnerability to sustained rises in benefit outflows. This approach to evidence-based decision-making in public insurance systems is scalable, interpretable, and policy-relevant because it combines classical statistical inference with modern computational approaches.

title: Artificial Intelligence Modelling of Non-Fourier Heat Transport in Magnetite-Graphene Hybrid Nanofluid for Sensor Applications
abstract: Magnetite (Iron Oxide) -Graphene hybrid nanoparticles, in particular, are found to be very beneficial for sensor surface applications because of their superior thermal conductivity, magnetic responsiveness, and enhanced heat transfer capability, which enhances the thermal stability, sensitivity, and operational efficiency of contemporary biosensors, microelectronic sensing devices, and smart sensors. This work delves into the dynamics of a magnetite-graphene/water-ethylene glycol hybrid nanofluid's unsteady MHD squeezed flow across a porous sensor surface under the conditions of viscous dissipation, nonlinear thermal radiation, and the non-Fourier C-C heat flux model. Applying the right transformations reduces the system of governing partial DEs to a set of ordinary DEs. These are then resolved by use of the MATLAB BVP5C solvers. After that, we'll use the numerical dataset to train two artificial neural networks: LMBP. This study's results show that the LMBP network replicates the BVP5C solution at epoch 77 with a gradient of (:7.17.10⁻⁸), a best validation MSE of (:1.77.10⁻¹⁰), and a correlation value (:R=1). Furthermore, As (:R:)and(::Ec) parameter values rise, the temperature profile (:θ:łeft(η:i̊ght)) also increases. Radiative heating and viscous dissipation are improved thermal conductivity.

title: Formation of Gradient Residual Stress in Ultrasonic Vibration-Assisted End Grinding Inconel 718: Microscopic Mechanism and Modeling
abstract: Residual stress (RS) on machined surfaces critically influences in-service performance. However, the underlying microscopic physical mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. The plastic deformation behavior under different parameters in ultrasonic vibration-assisted end grinding (UVAEG) was systematically investigated by RS characterization, in-situ grinding force measurement, and subsurface microstructure observation. An evaluation method for RS on machined surfaces was proposed. A prediction model for RS on machined surfaces was established based on dislocation pile-up theory. The microscopic mechanism of RS formation was analyzed. The effects of spindle speed and grinding depth on plastic deformation depth and the formation of gradient RS were also systematically studied. The results show that surface RS is positively correlated with dislocation density. The residual stress induced by grinding primarily originates from local stress fields generated by microstructural defects within the material. A larger plastic deformation depth is favorable for the formation of a deeper RS affected layer. Lower spindle speed and larger cutting depth can generate higher grinding forces, thereby promoting dislocation multiplication and migration, increasing the degree of lattice distortion and the depth of the affected layer, and consequently resulting in higher residual stress and a deeper affected layer. This study elucidates the microscopic mechanisms underlying internal stress formation at machined surfaces and provides a theoretical basis for optimizing machining processes to control material performance effectively.

title: Universal RKKY-like Interactions Between Tilted Skyrmions in Chiral Magnets
abstract: Skyrmion-skyrmion interaction is a fundamental problem that remains inadequately understood. Here we demonstrate that the interaction between two tilted skyrmions in a chiral magnetic film is intrinsically anisotropic, non-central, and oscillatory. This interaction varies periodically from repulsion to attraction with the skyrmion-skyrmion separation along a specified direction, resembling the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction observed between localized spins in metals. Our analysis reveals the underlying physics of a previously unrecognized universal wavy tail in the skyrmion spin texture. Importantly, the resulting RKKY-like interaction is universal for all tilted skyrmions, regardless of whether the tilt arises from an external field or crystalline magnetic anisotropy. These findings introduce a novel physical principle for designing skyrmion molecules or skyrmion superstructures, which have significant potential for applications in skyrmion-based spintronics and neuromorphic computing.

title: Negative temperature coefficient of Gilbert damping in magnetic bilayers
abstract: Author(s): Lulu Cao, Yuting Gong, Xianyang Lu, Yongbing Xu, Ya Zhai, Jing Wu, Roy W. Chantrell, and Richard F. L. Evans In simple metallic magnets, the intrinsic Gilbert damping increases with temperature and diverges near the Curie temperature as a result of spin fluctuations. Here, the authors find surprising and opposite behavior in Py/Nd bilayers, where the Gilbert damping decreases with increasing temperature and can be controlled by varying the thickness of the Nd capping layer. Their findings present a new spintronic spin-pumping effect that can be used to modify the dynamic properties of nanoscale devices for improved switching dynamics. [Phys. Rev. B 113, L220409] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026

title: Finite-bath open quantum systems: Exact dynamics
abstract: In this study, we introduce a method for deriving exact master equations from the dynamical map for finite open quantum systems coupled to (in)finite reservoirs, using the principle of minimal dissipation. The exact dynamics of the central spin model, which models a finite-bath open quantum system, is developed for two interaction types: Heisenberg and stochastic pure-dephasing interactions. The Heisenberg interaction yields a novel phase-covariant quantum channel in the strong-coupling regime, offering a new platform for studying a range of quantum information protocols. The stochastic pure-dephasing interaction provides the microscopic derivation of the paradigmatic non-Markovian random telegraph noise (RTN) channel, establishing its quantum foundation and offering insight into stochastic couplings. We derive the closed-form master equations for both models. As a demonstration, we explore the thermodynamic performance of these systems as quantum batteries. A direct relationship between quantum heat current and charging power is revealed, and RTN quantum batteries are shown to have advantages in charge storage.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Electronic orbital response to static magnetic fields. II. A general theoretical method
abstract: As a part of an ongoing project devoted to the development of theoretical foundations and computational methods for treating systems in external electro-magnetic fields, we present a new method here for dealing with magnetic fields of arbitrary strength and for arbitrary systems. The method is based on leaving the commonly used Coulomb gauge and instead introducing an operator gauge. We show that this method avoids the obstacles related with using the Coulomb gauge in combination with GIAOs (gauge-invariant atomic orbitals) as basis functions, i.e., complicated matrix elements and oscillatory behavior for non-magnetic terms. Moreover, our approach shares many features with the “Modern Theory of Magnetization,” which is based on the operator, ∇⃗k. However, our approach is not restricted to periodic systems and avoids many complications involved in the application of ∇⃗k. Our method is applicable for any system and field strength, and it readily provides an answer to the question of whether there is a surface/shape contribution to intensive magnetic responses for large systems. Test calculations on H2+ using a homemade ab initio program developed for small systems, and a simplified model for large systems, give mutually consistent and complementary results in support of our suggested approach, but not in complete agreement with results of GIAO calculations. We present a detailed analysis of this finding.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Spectral convergence of sum-of-Gaussians tensor neural networks for many-electron Schrödinger equation
abstract: An improved version of the sum-of-Gaussians tensor neural network (SOG-TNN) architecture is presented for solving the many-electron Schrödinger equation for one-dimensional soft-Coulomb systems. Model reduction techniques are introduced to reduce the number of tensor-factorized bases under the SOG approximation of the kernel. The Slater determinant ansatz is employed so that the antisymmetric property of the wave function can be strictly preserved. Numerical results show that the SOG-TNN achieves high accuracy with remarkably small basis sizes. Robust spectral convergence with respect to the basis size is also observed, consistently characterized by a mixed algebraic-exponential model for the error decay. These findings validate that the SOG-TNN architecture provides an ultra-efficient and low-rank representation of complex multi-electron wave functions, shedding light on high-fidelity quantum calculations in larger-scale many-electron systems.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
ai_explanation: 该论文明确提出张量神经网络求解多电子 Schrödinger 方程，是 AI/神经网络与量子化学、计算物理的直接交叉。高度符合 AI4Science。
ai_detailed_summary: 研究对象是一维软 Coulomb 多电子体系的 Schrödinger 方程求解。论文提出改进的 sum-of-Gaussians 张量神经网络结构，并使用模型降阶减少核函数近似下的张量分解基数量。方法中结合 Slater 行列式 Ansatz，以严格保持波函数的反对称性质。结果显示该 SOG-TNN 在较小基组规模下实现高精度和稳健的谱收敛，为神经网络量子多体求解提供了有价值路径。

title: Elucidating the synergetic interplay between average intermolecular coupling and coupling disorder in short-time exciton transfer
abstract: Exciton transport in molecular aggregates is a fundamental process governing the performance of organic optoelectronics and light-harvesting systems. While most theoretical studies have emphasized long-time transport behavior, recent advances in ultrafast spectroscopy have brought into focus the short-time regime, in which exciton motion remains ballistic on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. In this work, we develop an analytical framework for short-time exciton dynamics in a one-dimensional lattice subject to both on-site energetic (diagonal) disorder and intermolecular coupling (off-diagonal) fluctuations. Utilizing the reciprocal-space analysis, we derive closed-form expressions for the first and second spatial moments considering both localized excitation and moving Gaussian initial conditions. Our analytical and numerical results show that, while the long-time dynamics are influenced by diagonal disorder, the short-time ballistic expansion is governed primarily by off-diagonal disorder. Crucially, we reveal a synergistic interplay between the average intermolecular coupling and the off-diagonal coupling disorder strength, demonstrating that they contribute equivalently to short-time exciton transport. Moreover, we integrate this generic disorder model with a realistic molecular system within the framework of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for characterizing and optimizing ultrafast energy flow of disordered molecular aggregates in complex dielectric media.
